newsitem.title: USA: Emerging market debt slides with U.S. Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market debt slides with U.S. Treasuries.

text.p: A volatile U.S. Treasuries market sent emerging market debts spinning lower in moderate trading, market sources said.
"We saw some net selling," said a Brady trader at a European bank, "but dealers still dominated the market."
Fund managers were reluctant to spoil the record achieved so far this year to venture into the market, he said.
No news in particular from emerging markets precipitated the mood change, they said, putting the blame squarely on the less certain outlook for U.S. interest rates.
"There's not a lot of optimism," said another trader. "People are less confident than a week ago."
Yield spreads over U.S. Treasuries widened on average about 5 basis points, which had been larger earlier when the Treasuries were trading in the plus territory, he said.
While the losses appeared small, the gyrations were unnerving, the trader said.
The most liquid Brazil C BR8D14=RR and Argentina FRBs ARFLC05=RR came under pressure, and the worst hit were the Bulgarian papers.
Both Brazil C and Argie FRB lost 3/8 to bid 71-1/4 and 84-3/8.
Bulgaria took another blow on the heel of Wednesday's losses. Bulgaria FLRB BGFLIRG=RR fell 1/2 to 37-5/8 bid, and IAB BGFLTH11=RR plunged 1-1/2 to bid 49-7/8.
Traders said most of the price decline took place in earlier London trading.
